title: WAF ruleset deploy with a catastrophically backtracking regex saturates edge CPU
source_note: Failure pattern and root-cause shape are drawn from the Cloudflare 2019-07-02 outage (a WAF rule containing a pathological regex drove global CPU exhaustion). Service names, log lines, metrics, timestamps, and commit hash are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~13:42 UTC the edge tier is serving a high rate of 502s for a large fraction of all traffic. Customer reports came in within a few minutes. No known infrastructure maintenance was scheduled. Edge hosts look CPU-bound.

signal_lines.msg: cpu usage 78% and rising on all workers
worker CPU saturated; request queue growing (depth=4100)
returning 502: no worker capacity to accept connection
regex evaluation exceeded 40ms budget on managed rule 100417 (pattern contains nested quantifiers: (?:.*.*=.*))
operator initiated rollback to previous WAF ruleset
cpu usage 24%; 5xx rate falling back toward baseline

deploys.summary: roll out WAF managed ruleset 2026.05.12 (adds ~30 new rules, incl. rule 100417)

ground_truth.root_cause: A newly deployed WAF managed-rule set (commit 7f3a9c1) contained a rule (100417) with a catastrophically backtracking regular expression. Evaluating that pattern against normal request traffic drove edge-proxy worker CPU to saturation within about a minute, so requests queued and then failed with 502s across effectively all traffic.
evidence_path: deploy 7f3a9c1 to edge-proxy at 13:42 rolls out a new WAF managed ruleset
edge-proxy CPU climbs from ~35% to 100% beginning ~13:42:20, immediately after the deploy
waf-engine ERROR at 13:44:30: regex evaluation exceeded its time budget on managed rule 100417 (nested quantifiers)
edge-proxy 5xx rate rises to ~62% as workers saturate and the request queue grows
CPU and 5xx rate recover after the WAF ruleset is rolled back at ~13:52
ground_truth.fix: Roll back the WAF ruleset to the previous version. Add a regex-complexity / backtracking check and a per-rule CPU budget to the rule-deployment pipeline, and canary WAF rule changes on a small fraction of traffic before global rollout.
